title: Data Access Certification & Retention Escrow — proposal
body:
Purpose and context:
This draft proposes a short-form contractual clause and operational runbook for (i) certification of data access events and (ii) a limited retention escrow (evidence escrow) tied to on-prem and private deployments of Redwood inference. Aim is to give customers a bounded way to obtain third-party-verifiable records for compliance/legal needs while minimizing long-term retention risk for Redwood.

Key objectives (design principles):
- Time-boxed: escrowed artifacts are retained only for a narrowly scoped period (default 90 days) unless the customer triggers a preservation request.
- Minimal content: store metadata/transactional logs and redacted payloads rather than full user content unless strictly required and mutually agreed.
- Verifiability: artifacts should be cryptographically stamped and accompanied by a tamper-evident manifest for independent audit.
- Operational controls: well-defined access request, approval workflow, and emergency suspension process.

Definitions (working):
- "Evidence Escrow Vault": a secured storage location (customer-managed S3-compatible or Redwood-hosted sealed store) where preserved artifacts are placed.
- "Certified Access Report (CAR)": a signed package including event metadata, cryptographic checksum(s), access-control snapshot, and operator attestations for a given time window.
- "Retention Window": the default period that artifacts are kept in the Evidence Escrow Vault (proposed: 90 days).
- "Preservation Trigger": an authenticated customer request (legal hold, litigation hold, regulatory inquiry) that extends retention for specified items.

Draft clause (contract language — short form):
1) Escrowed Artifacts. Vendor shall place, for the Retention Window, a copy of the artifacts specified in Schedule A ("Escrowed Artifacts") into the Evidence Escrow Vault. Escrowed Artifacts will be limited to: service logs, index-level metadata, access-control snapshots, and redacted request identifiers. Full request payloads will not be escrowed unless Customer provides written authorization in Schedule A.

2) Retention Window and Preservation. The standard Retention Window is ninety (90) days from time of creation. Customer may issue a Preservation Trigger in writing to extend retention for specific Escrowed Artifacts subject to Section 4 (Fees and access). Any extension will be narrow in scope and include an end date or event that terminates the hold.

3) Certification Package. For any Customer-requested CAR, Vendor will provide a signed Certification Package within ten (10) business days. The package will include: (a) event metadata (timestamps, node/region, request id), (b) a cryptographic digest of the stored artifact, (c) an operator attestation describing the preservation process, and (d) the Evidence Escrow Vault manifest. Vendor’s signature will use key material under Vendor control unless Customer requests use of a mutually trusted signing key (see Schedule B).

4) Access and Audit Rights. Customer’s authorized auditor may inspect CARs and request a one-time on-site or remote verification session. Audit scope must be pre-approved and limited to the specific Escrowed Artifacts identified in the Preservation Trigger. Vendor will not disclose customer-created content beyond redactions agreed in Schedule A without Customer’s written consent or lawful process.

5) Sequestration and Emergency Suspension. If Vendor reasonably suspects unauthorized exfiltration or other compromise, Vendor may: (a) suspend writing new Escrowed Artifacts to the Evidence Escrow Vault, (b) freeze retrieval access pending investigation, and (c) provide interim CARs describing the incident. Vendor will notify Customer within forty-eight (48) hours of reasonable belief of compromise and provide remediation steps and timeline.

6) Fees. Standard retention and CAR generation are included up to [X] CARs/month. Additional preservation requests or extended retention will be charged per Schedule C (operational fees). Fee negotiation points: threshold before fee applies, carveouts for production incidents.

7) Data Minimization and Redaction. Vendor will apply agreed redaction rules (Schedule A) to minimize personal data exposure in escrow. Customer and Vendor will jointly adopt a redaction baseline during onboarding; deviation requires mutual agreement.

8) Termination and Disposal. Upon expiration of the Retention Window (or termination of all preservation holds), Vendor will securely delete Escrowed Artifacts and produce a Proof of Destruction certificate signed by an authorized operator. Proofs will include checksum of the deleted objects and time of deletion.

Operational runbook (practical steps — internal notes):
- Onboarding checklist:
  - Confirm customer choice: customer-managed vault (preferred) vs Redwood-hosted sealed vault.
  - Populate Schedule A (artifact granularity) and Schedule B (signing key options).
  - Capture redaction profile and legal contacts for preservation triggers.
  - Create JIRA ticket with tag SEC-ESCROW onboard-<customer>.

- Preservation request flow:
  1) Customer sends Preservation Trigger to security-escrow@redwood.ai and copies legal@customerdomain.
  2) Escrow owner (security) opens a triage call within 4 business hours.
  3) Security engages infra to snapshot manifest and generate CAR.
  4) Legal assesses scope and confirms fees/hold duration.
  5) Vendor uploads CAR to Evidence Escrow Vault and notifies Customer with retrieval instructions.

- CAR generation checklist (operator):
  - Identify artifact IDs and compute SHA256 digests.
  - Export access-control snapshot (IAM/ACL state) for time window.
  - Record infra node/region and operator steps with timestamps.
  - Apply redaction script to payloads if required and store redaction log.
  - Sign package with escrow-signing key and produce manifest.

Negotiation notes / bargaining chips (internal):
- Customers often push for longer default retention (180-365 days). Push back with: increased cost, increased legal risk, and propose targeted holds instead.
- For high-sensitivity customers, prefer customer-managed vault + customer signing key. This reduces vendor liability and is a strong win for customers but raises onboarding friction.
- Offer tiered pricing: baseline (90d, 3 CARs/mo), premium (180d, 12 CARs/mo), enterprise (custom).

Open questions and TODOs:
- Decide default fee thresholds (e.g., 1 free CAR per 30 days per account? tie to committed spend?) -- ACTION: finance + legal to propose pricing band by 2026-03-01.
- Implementation: do we use separate KMS keys per customer for evidence signing or a multi-tenant signing service? ACTION: infra to prototype customer-key option (JIRA-SEC-234).
- Legal review: add language about lawful process vs. customer consent for disclosure. ACTION: Legal to draft final carveouts by next review.

Quick decision log (history of edits):
- 2025-11-08: initial draft by Ava.
- 2025-12-16: added Preservation Trigger workflow (Marcus).
- 2026-01-10: inserted sequestration notification SLA (Sofia).
- 2026-02-21: updated CAR timeline and retention default (Ethan).

Appendix A — Schedule A (example artifact list, to be customized per customer):
- Service log index entries (timestamp, request id, model id, token count)
- Request metadata (redacted client IP, region, route)
- Access-control snapshot (roles, policies active)
- Redacted payloads only if customer authorizes, with redaction rules enumerated

Appendix B — Example Preservation Trigger template (email):
Subject: Preservation Trigger — [Customer] — Escrow artifacts for [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
Body:
  1) Customer name and account id
  2) Artifact identifiers or selection criteria (time range, request ids, model id)
  3) Intended retention extension and reason (litigation/regulatory/investigation)
  4) Contact/legal POC and signature

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the default retention short; we don't want a proliferation of long-lived evidence stores.
- Make customer-managed vault the recommended default in sales materials — reduces friction on sensitive customers.
- Build a small UI in console to request CARs and track Preservation Triggers (saves ops emails).

Attachment checklist for negotiation:
- Draft Schedule A (per-customer)
- Schedule B: key management options
- Sample CAR (redacted) for customer review
- Pricing bands for retention and CARs

End of draft.
